title: Neuroinformatics and the Brain
answer: Brain computer interfaces, dementia signals, functional MRI, seizure prediction and cognitive rehabilitation.

children.name: Brain Computer Interfaces
children.blurb: Brain computer interfaces are systems that read neural signals and translate them into commands for external devices, or stimulate the brain in response to computed intent.

children.name: Early Signals of Dementia
children.blurb: Early signals of dementia in AI work cover the subtle changes in speech, memory, gait, sleep, and daily activity that may appear years before a formal diagnosis.

children.name: Functional MRI Interpretation
children.blurb: Functional MRI interpretation uses AI to map brain activity from blood oxygen level dependent signals, turning four dimensional scans into maps of networks, task activation, and resting state connectivity.

children.name: Seizure Prediction
children.blurb: Seizure prediction is the use of machine learning to forecast epileptic seizures before clinical onset, typically from continuous electroencephalography or wearable signals.

children.name: Cognitive Rehabilitation
children.blurb: Cognitive rehabilitation uses structured exercises and compensatory strategies to improve attention, memory, executive function, language, and social cognition after acquired brain injury, stroke, or in progressive conditions.

sections.body: Neuroinformatics and the brain applies artificial intelligence to data from the nervous system, including electrical signals, brain scans, and behavioral measures. Current work includes decoding intended hand or speech movements from implanted or wearable sensors for brain computer interfaces, analyzing speech and typing patterns for early signs of dementia, and reading functional MRI scans to map brain activity. AI is also being used to flag patterns in EEG recordings that may precede a seizure, and to adjust cognitive training tasks based on a person's performance. These are real, working systems in research clinics and some approved devices, not just lab concepts. The focus is on measurement and pattern recognition, not on replacing a neurologist.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has made real progress in narrow tasks. Seizure prediction models can often detect pre seizure brain activity minutes before an event in hospital monitoring, but false alarms remain common outside controlled settings. Brain computer interfaces have allowed people with paralysis to move a cursor or type at slow speeds, yet long term reliability and daily use are still limited. Dementia signal tools can flag subtle changes in voice or typing, but they are screening aids, not diagnoses, and they can be wrong for many people. Functional MRI interpretation models can label brain regions and some conditions, but they do not yet explain cause and effect. The honest limit is that most of these systems work best on clean, standardized data from a single clinic, and they degrade on messy real world data. This site tracks 1000 medical AI models overall, and the brain focused tools here are a small, uneven part of that count.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how AI reads intent from the nervous system should start with Brain Computer Interfaces, which covers implanted and external sensors and what they can currently control. Early Signals of Dementia explains the passive monitoring tools that look at speech, typing, and daily activity, and it pairs naturally with Cognitive Rehabilitation, which covers software that adapts memory and attention exercises. Functional MRI Interpretation sits between them, focused on brain scans rather than electrical or behavioral data, and it is the page to consult for questions about imaging based biomarkers. Seizure Prediction is the most clinically urgent page, describing EEG based warning systems and their current reliability. Together these five pages move from direct neural control, to passive screening, to imaging, to forecasting, and finally to training, but each page stands alone for a specific question.
